subject: Mythology
title: Why We Still Need Mythological Creatures
description: A fast breakdown of Why We Still Need Mythological Creatures for builders.

hook.text: Dragons, phoenixes, and werewolves have survived for thousands of years. They must serve a purpose beyond entertainment.

buildup.text: Mythological creatures externalize fears: dragons are greed, werewolves are savagery, vampires are predatory desire.

discovery.text: Carl Jung called them archetypes — universal symbols that emerge from the collective unconscious of all humanity.

twist.text: New creatures keep being invented: Slender Man, the Backrooms, and SCP entries are mythology being written in real time.

climax.text: Humans cannot stop making monsters because monsters help us understand the parts of ourselves we cannot face directly.

punchline.text: Every monster is a mirror. We keep inventing them because we need to see.

quiz.question: Why do mythological creatures persist across all human cultures?
options: Because ancient people saw real creatures that have since gone extinct
They externalize human fears and function as mirrors for understanding ourselves
Religious institutions preserve them for ceremonial purposes
